approved: Anti-Money Laundering and Counter-Terrorism Financing Amendment (Making Gambling Businesses Accountable) Bill 2020
Written by a model from the explanatory memorandum; not the record
This bill would make gambling businesses report to AUSTRAC if they suspect a customer is using illegally obtained money to gamble.
It would also let the Federal Court order gambling companies to compensate victims when a bettor used illegal funds to pay for gambling services.
The bill would amend relevant legislation to impose a positive obligation on gambling entities and prevent them profiting from illegal behaviour.
Gambling companies must report suspicious payments to AUSTRAC.
The Federal Court can order gambling companies to compensate injured parties for losses from illegal funds.
Gambling entities are prevented from profiting from illegal behaviour.
Gambling businesses and companies that provide gambling services.

The speaker seconded a bill to make gambling businesses liable for accepting stolen money, citing $25 billion in annual Australian gambling losses and the case of Gavin Fineff, who stole $8.4 million from clients. The bill would allow the Federal Court to order gambling companies to compensate victims of crimes funding bets.
